notes: Intro: Galena builds autonomous warehouse routing + voice ops for 3PLs. Looking to replace an in-house LLM proxy with a predictable dedicated stack.
Primary ask: dedicated capacity that guarantees throughput for gateway-level routing decisions (low jitter) + p95 latency SLOs for agent chat.
Baseline metrics provided by customer (from internal qps telemetry): steady-state 420 QPS for micro-requests (short prompts), peak up to 1.6k QPS during batch job windows.
Token characteristics: avg prompt 60 tokens, avg completion 120 tokens -> ~180 tokens per request. Peak token/sec estimate ~288k tokens/sec at 1.6k QPS.
Redwood Evaluate: demo cluster ran open-weights Llama-2-70B-8bit equiv; observed 210 QPS per A100-80GB equiv under continuous batching (chat style).
Desired sizing: customer expects reserved pool equivalent to 8 x A100-80GB (or 12 x H100 small instances) to meet steady-state with 2x headroom for KV cache warmups.
Throughput guarantees: wants contractual throughput guarantee for steady-state (>=400 QPS sustained) and defined degradation policy during peaks.
Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for agent chat (context length 1k tokens), tail objectives negotiable - customer expects credits if p95 breached more than 3x/month.
Autoscale expectations: burst capacity to +2x for <30m allowed, but must be explicit how fallback model variants are routed during scale events.
Cache strategy: prefix/KV cache reuse critical to hit targets — want guidance on model pinning and cache warmup for rolling deploys.
Security: require KMS integration for model keys, audit logs forwarded to SIEM, SAML SSO for console access. Data residency: EU workload must remain in eu-west region.
Procurement notes: legal flagged indemnity clause and data residency paragraph. Procurement expects final SOW and price by 2026-03-22.
Quote from Dir. of Platform: "We need deterministic unit economics — if cost per effective token varies too much we can't commit to a reserve."
Action items so far: completed network pre-check (SRE), demo of dedicated instance sizing, Redwood to schedule 4-hour on-site workshop with infra + SRE + platform owners.
Workshop goals: validate baseline QPS, run tokenized replay of 48-hour production window, estimate reserved GPU count & autoscale policy, draft SLA wording for throughput/latency credits.
POC plan: 6-week proof on Dedicated pool; week1: traffic mirror + KV cache tuning; week2-3: load tests at 1x/1.5x/2x steady; week4: resilience and failover; final report + cost model.
Risks noted: live traffic replay requires approval; on-prem rack power constraints could limit H100 deployment density in one site.
Decision criteria: predictable latency SLOs, transparent cost per effective request, ability to host private plane in EU, 99.9% uptime SLA for dedicated pool.
Next meeting: on-site sizing workshop scheduled 2026-03-18 (SRE + infra + AE + SE) — SE to bring load-testing scripts and expected tokenized trace.
Jira ref for infra action items: INF-8472 (network peering), SEC-6610 (kms integration), OPS-9021 (maintenance window cadence).
Misc: customer is price-sensitive on burst pricing — asked for example billing model showing sustained vs burst charges.
Follow-up: Redwood to deliver preliminary GPU sizing + cost model and proposed SLA draft within 7 business days after workshop.
Status summary: technically qualified; procurement/security blocks remaining; timeline aggressive (contract target Q2 2026).
Competing options: continuing current internal proxy (cheap but brittle) or switching to cloud-managed endpoints (higher per-token cost, lower control).
